subject: Re: BrightGrid SLA packaging — hybrid uptime + response pricing
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightgrid.io>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@brightgrid.com, marta.lemos@brightgrid.com
Date: Fri, 20 Apr 2028 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: BrightGrid — SLA packaging question

Hi Olga,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We loved the latency characteristics and the model routing controls. Procurement asked me to follow up on the SLA/pricing side so we can lock internal approvals. Two specific asks: 1) can you outline how a hybrid uptime + response-time package would be priced (we want a mix of 99.95% uptime for critical endpoints and a faster response lane for P1s), and 2) what's the discount if we commit to a 12-month Dedicated capacity with a 30% uplift for peak months?

Also wondering what the escalation coverage looks like for after-hours incidents and whether Redwood provides a named escalation lead for enterprise customers. If you can send a short matrix (uptime bands, response windows, credits) and a sample SOW we can circulate to legal/procurement, that would be great.

Best,
Samir
Head of Platform, BrightGrid

[Attachment: BrightGrid_Requirements_Summary.docx (docx)]

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightgrid.io>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightGrid — SLA packaging question

Samir —

Thanks for the clear asks. We're happy to put together a concise matrix and a draft SOW. Quick answers up front while we prepare the docs:

- Hybrid pricing: we price uptime tiers as a % overlay on base usage (e.g., 99.9% baseline; 99.95% +6% monthly fee; 99.99% +15% monthly fee). The fast-response lane is a per-seat/per-route premium (flat fee per critical route) or a retainer-style oncall seat; can be structured either as credits or guaranteed P1 response SLA.

- Commit discount: for a 12-month Dedicated commit we typically offer a 20% baseline discount on usage plus a step-up credit for predictable peak-month burst capacity. A 30% contractual uplift for known peak months can be accommodated with a reduced uplift charge (we'd discount the uplift fee by 10 points at that commit level).

- Escalation coverage: enterprise customers get a named escalation lead, 24x7 on-call for P1s (with an assigned rotation), and a playbook that includes regional failover policies. After-hours coverage is included in the higher-tier response plan; alternately we can provide a limited-hours plan plus on-call retainer.

I'll attach a short SLA matrix and a draft SOW — please review and tell us any must-haves for legal/procurement. Aditya & Marissa: can you confirm the discount math and whether we want to present the response lane as "retainer seats" or "per-route premium" to BrightGrid?

Thanks —
Olga
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: initial-SLA-matrix.pdf (pdf)]

From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 23 Apr 2028 10:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightGrid — SLA packaging question

Olga — quick internal note before we send official numbers to BrightGrid:

- For a 12-month Dedicated commit the commercial baseline is 20% off list. For the explicit 30% planned uplift months we can treat those as pre-funded burst credits at a 15% uplift charge rather than the normal 25% burst premium — effectively BrightGrid would pay 15% extra for tokens in uplift months. This makes the overall blended discount close to 22-24% depending on uplift size.

- Response lane: recommend framing as a retainer model (named seats) with an option to convert to per-route premium if they prefer predictability. Retainer seats are simpler for legal and easier to quantify in the SOW. Seat pricing for 24x7 P1 cover: $8k/month per seat (covers rotation + named escalation lead + post-incident RCA). 9-5 fast-response lane: $3k/month per seat.

- Credits: uptime credits are tiered. 99.95% = 5% credit, 99.9% = 10% credit, <99.5% triggers higher remediation. We'll map these to their critical endpoints in the matrix.

Jonas: flag any legal friction on the seat wording and whether the named escalation lead language is okay.

-Aditya
Senior Solutions, Redwood Inference

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, olga.petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 24 Apr 2028 11:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightGrid — SLA packaging question

Aditya/Olga —

High level legal notes:

- "Named escalation lead" should be described as a named contact for incident triage and escalation; avoid language that implies a single-person guarantee (use rotation + primary contact). We'll include substitution/resignation language and 30-day notice for lead changes.

- Retainer seats: define scope clearly (number of incidents covered per month before overage, means of contact, expected response times). Avoid absolute uptime credits beyond agreed thresholds — keep caps on aggregate credit liability (standard is a percentage of monthly recurring revenue tied to the commitment).

- Proposal should call out a 30-day service provisioning window for Dedicated capacity and a pre-funded burst pool drawdown mechanism tied to usage reporting.

I can draft the legal bullet points to append to the SOW.

-Jonas
Head of Commercial Contracts, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightgrid.io>
Cc: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai, procurement@brightgrid.com
Date: Wed, 25 Apr 2028 14:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: BrightGrid — SLA packaging question

Samir —

Appended below is a short proposal summary and attached artifacts. We tried to keep the SOW bulleted and the pricing matrix transparent so your procurement/legal teams can review quickly. If helpful we can run a 30-minute walk-through with legal next week.

Summary proposal (high level):
- Commitment: 12-month Dedicated capacity (committed baseline).
- Commercial: 20% committed usage discount off hosted list; uplift months (pre-committed 30% monthly capacity increase) billed at +15% uplift charge on usage consumed during those months.
- Hybrid uptime band: baseline platform SLA 99.9% included. Option to purchase 99.95% for +6% MRC or 99.99% for +15% MRC. Uptime credits: 99.95% = 5% credit, 99.9% = 10% credit (applied to monthly bill); credit caps = 50% of monthly committed fees.
- Response coverage: recommended retainer seats. 24x7 P1 seat = $8k/month; 9-5 P1 seat = $3k/month. Seats include named escalation contact (rotation), RCA delivery within 72 hours for P1s, and quarterly operational playbook review. Additional incident overage priced at $1,200/incident after included incidents.
- Onboarding & provisioning: 30-day capacity provision window after contract signature; initial SOW deliverables include playbook, escalation roster, and test failover runbook.

Attachments: initial-SLA-matrix.pdf, BrightGrid_SOW_v3.pdf, SLA-pricing-grid.xlsx, Redwood-Response-Ladder.pdf

Next steps: please confirm whether procurement wants the retainer seat model or per-route premium by EOD Friday; if they want the retainer we will provide a sample SOW with seat counts and a redline-friendly commercial term sheet for legal. We can schedule a legal walkthrough on Tue/Wed next week.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0198
olga.petrov@redwood.ai
